rationale: This is the final iteration, so the priority is a robust, approvable build for the unseen track. The best measured design is iteration 6 (score 937.10), which iteration 10 reproduced exactly. It finished 60/60 across oval, s-bend and slalom (oval 944.7, s-bend 940.9, slalom 925.7). Every single-variable follow-up scored lower: kd 0.9 at y=0.06 gave 865.3, y=0.07 with kd 1.1 gave 930.9, and kd 1.1 at y=0.06 gave 925.9. kp 6 collapsed the oval and s-bend in iteration 4. Mass is already at its 0.40 kg floor, and body_width cannot change the off-track limit because the 0.06 m floor binds. I therefore resubmit the iteration 6 design unchanged. The remaining loss is slalom line-loss events (about 0.65 per run), but no tested single change has reduced it without a cost elsewhere, so an untested tweak now would risk the unseen-track result for little expected gain. Expected result: about 937 on the development tracks with 60/60 finishes. Hypotheses for the record: (a) the design generalises to the unseen track because its margin is wide on all three shapes; (b) line-loss events remain the largest recoverable term. Measurements wanted: per-track completion, max_error, line_loss_events, completion_time, steering_oscillation and noise_robustness, to check how much of the margin survives on a different shape.
